## Question and approach

This notebook asks whether firms with better-than-expected H-1B lottery outcomes submit more or fewer registrations in the following lottery year. It is the baseline analysis for the industry-heterogeneity notebook.

The unit of observation is an employer EIN in a lottery year. Lottery luck is the firm's selection-rate surprise relative to that year's national selection rate, measured in 10-percentage-point units (`selection_luck_10pp`). The analysis uses the full H-1B employer participation panel; it is not restricted to Compustat-matched public firms.

Two next-year outcomes capture different margins of participation:

- `log(1 + next_year_registrations)`: whether firms file more or fewer registrations, while retaining firms with zero filings next year.
- `returns_next_year`: whether firms file at least one registration next year.

The log outcome reduces the influence of very large filers. Its coefficient is an approximate proportional change in `1 +` next-year registrations, not a raw count change. The return indicator provides a complementary extensive-margin estimate.

## Load the saved participation panel

```{r}
#| label: load-data

library(dplyr)
library(fixest)
library(broom)
library(knitr)

participation_path <- file.path("data", "h1b_lottery_participation_panel.rds")
stopifnot(file.exists(participation_path))
participation <- readRDS(participation_path)

required_variables <- c(
  "ein", "lottery_year", "n_registrations", "selection_luck_10pp",
  "next_year_registrations", "returns_next_year",
  "log_current_registrations", "log_next_year_registrations"
)
stopifnot(all(required_variables %in% names(participation)))
```

## Descriptive sample summary

```{r}
#| label: descriptive-summary

participation |>
  summarise(
    firm_years = n(), firms = n_distinct(ein),
    current_registrations = sum(n_registrations),
    next_year_registrations = sum(next_year_registrations),
    return_rate = mean(returns_next_year),
    mean_lottery_luck_10pp = mean(selection_luck_10pp)
  ) |>
  mutate(return_rate = scales::percent(return_rate, accuracy = 0.1)) |>
  kable(caption = "Full H-1B employer participation panel")
```

## Lottery luck and next-year participation

For each outcome, estimate:

\[
Y_{i,t+1} = \beta\,\text{lottery luck}_{it} +
\gamma\log(1 + \text{current registrations}_{it}) +
\text{lottery-year fixed effects} + e_{it}.
\]

Lottery-year fixed effects account for annual changes in the national H-1B registration environment. Standard errors are clustered by firm EIN. The control for current registrations compares firms with similar current filing scale.

```{r}
#| label: estimate-baseline-models

outcomes <- c(
  log_next_year_registrations = "Log(1 + next-year registrations)",
  returns_next_year = "Returns to lottery next year"
)

estimate_participation_model <- function(outcome_name, outcome_label) {
  model_data <- participation |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[outcome_name]]), !is.na(selection_luck_10pp),
      !is.na(log_current_registrations))
  model <- feols(
    as.formula(paste0(outcome_name,
      " ~ selection_luck_10pp + log_current_registrations | lottery_year")),
    data = model_data, cluster = ~ein
  )
  luck_term <- tidy(model) |> filter(term == "selection_luck_10pp")
  tibble(
    outcome = outcome_label, firm_years = nobs(model),
    firms = n_distinct(model_data$ein),
    luck_coefficient = luck_term$estimate, std_error = luck_term$std.error,
    conf_low = luck_term$estimate - 1.96 * luck_term$std.error,
    conf_high = luck_term$estimate + 1.96 * luck_term$std.error,
    p_value = luck_term$p.value
  )
}

baseline_results <- bind_rows(lapply(names(outcomes), function(outcome_name) {
  estimate_participation_model(outcome_name, outcomes[[outcome_name]])
}))

baseline_results |>
  mutate(
    across(c(luck_coefficient, std_error, conf_low, conf_high), ~ round(.x, 3)),
    p_value = signif(p_value, 3)
  ) |>
  kable(caption = "Lottery luck and next-year H-1B participation")
```

## Interpretation

For the log-registration outcome, a positive coefficient means that a luckier lottery year is associated with a proportional increase in `1 +` next-year registrations; a negative coefficient means a proportional decrease. For the return outcome, the coefficient is a change in the probability of filing at least one registration next year.

The industry notebook, `h1b_sector_heterogeneity.qmd`, applies the same specification separately by industry in the Compustat-matched public-firm subset. Compare those exploratory industry estimates with this full-panel baseline before drawing conclusions about heterogeneous responses.
